newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty just weaker vs basket, depo rates stable.
newsitem.headline: Zloty just weaker vs basket, depo rates stable.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed slightly down against the basket of currencies as the afternoon fall of the dollar/mark did not offset early importers' currency purchases, dealers said.
They said small foreign entry into Polish T-bills at today's primary tender, estimated at $30 million, might have also contributed to the afternoon currency-selling trend.
"The zloty rebounded from early losses on afternoon currency-selling triggered by the falling dollar/mark," said Katarzyna Solarz from Pekao SA.

The zloty closed at 2.96/2.93 percent from the trading band centre, just down from Friday's 2.98/2.94 percent. It closed at 3.0748/60 to the dollar, up from 3.0885/95 on Friday and at 1.8220/25 to the mark, down from 1.8105/14.
Dealers said foreigners were currently not keen on Polish T-bills longer than 8-weeks as they did not expect any near-term cut in the zloty devaluation rate.
"With the lack of speculative possibilities because of the anchored zloty rate, foreign bids for high T-bill yields were not competitive today," said a dealer at a major Polish bank.
